lede: Buffalo carries a full EdgeDesk team rating at -9.6; Robert Morris is not one of the 138 FBS programmes EdgeDesk rates, so the comparison is one-sided by construction rather than by judgement.
EdgeDesk makes it Buffalo -16.1 before any sportsbook number is consulted, with Buffalo winning 86% of simulations.

The roster and position-group comparison below explains where EdgeDesk’s separation comes from on the side it can measure; Robert Morris is absent from the FBS player dataset, so the exact size of that gap is not established.
Data confidence on this matchup is 53% — enough to publish, not enough to treat the exact margin as settled.

advantages.note: An advantage is only claimed where BOTH teams carry a national rank in that category — the national rank is the one scale on which a QB room and a run defence are comparable. A category where one side is unrated appears here as a measurement and as uncertainty, never as an edge.

favourite.heading: Why Buffalo can pull away
bullets: Buffalo is the better football team by 14.7 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 64% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+14.7 pts).
Playing at Buffalo is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Robert Morris can keep it close
bullets: Stylistically the matchup favours Robert Morris by 2.7 points: pass rush vs pass protection (-2.7 pts).
The outcome range is 15.1 points wide at one sigma — p10 -6.9 to p90 +37.1 for Buffalo, so a projection of +16.1 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 3%.
50% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
Robert Morris is not in the FBS rating set, so EdgeDesk cannot measure what it does well. An unmeasured opponent is an unknown, not a weak one, and the size of the gap is not established.
